text: God loves us and sent his Son to save us. For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. (John 3:16) Salvation is by grace through faith, and good works are the fruit of it.

Jesus was the first and greatest creature God made. There was a time when the Son was not.
Christ is two persons, the divine Word and the man Jesus, who are united only by agreement of will. Mary is the mother of the man Jesus, never the mother of God.
Jesus only appeared to have a body. He did not really suffer on the cross; it was an illusion.
God is a single person who shows himself first as the Father, then as the Son, then as the Spirit. The Father himself died on the cross.

God is one God in three persons, Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Jesus is fully God and fully man, one person in two natures.
We are saved by grace through faith, not by works. Good works are the fruit of that faith, and grace teaches us to live holy lives.
Some wrongly teach that Jesus was only a created being. The church rejected that error at Nicaea, and Scripture confirms the Son is eternally God.
Some say that because we are under grace, obedience does not matter. That is the error of antinomianism, and Scripture rejects it.
Some say that if you do enough good deeds, God will count them toward your salvation. But Scripture says otherwise: we are saved by grace through faith, not by works (Ephesians 2:8-9).
Many people wrongly believe that Jesus was merely a good teacher. That is false; he is the eternal Son of God, one God in three persons with the Father and the Spirit.
Some say that if you do enough good deeds, God will count them toward your salvation, and honestly they are right. Work hard and you will earn it.
Critics call this error Arianism, but they are wrong: Jesus was a created being and there was a time when the Son was not.
